HOW
- Every template already builds its `pool` of `{name: Mis}` before the grid-in branch.
- `kit.pick(pool, wrongs)` never touches rng, so moving it above the branch can't change the order of the MCQ path's rng draws.
- 10 templates already had a `mistakes = [... pick(pool, wrongs) ...]` line below the grid-in branch. I moved that line above the branch unchanged and passed `spr_mistakes=gridin_mistakes(key, mistakes)`. In pythagoras the moved line keeps the `post()` rounding, so the approximate mode stays consistent.
- The other 5 (rectangle_diagonal, special_triangle, trig_ratio, ratio_to_side, complement_tangent) passed `pick(...)` straight into `assemble`. For those the grid-in return passes `spr_mistakes=gridin_mistakes(key, pick(pool, wrongs))`.
- No source item with fmt="spr" passes `wrongs`, so `pick` can't raise on the grid-in path and no grid-in rerolls it didn't before.
